solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 'Wet' encompasses a person with left-wing tendencies

indicators.note: the word for wet surrounds the article, holding it inside

parts.note: wet means damp, moist

explanation.surface: A damp, feeble politician turns out to harbour a leftie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' is British political slang for a moderate, which makes the surface sound like a party squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Mao Zedong's communism is a person of strongly left-wing views.

clue.text: Roadside feature upended German car in fog

indicators.note: the reversed car goes inside the word for fog

parts.note: fog is a thicker mist

indicators.note: in a down clue, upended means the car's name is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: Opel is a German car maker

explanation.surface: A German car has overturned in fog beside the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Opel is a German brand (sold as Vauxhall in Britain); in a down answer 'upended' means read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A marker post at the roadside showing distances in miles is a typical roadside feature.

clue.text: How it is when a left-winger pays repeatedly?

definitions.text: How it is when a left-winger pays
definitions.meaning: a Trot is a Trotskyist, so a bill footed by one is charged to that leftie

explanation.surface: A wry question about what happens when a socialist keeps picking up the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trot' is a familiar British slang term for a Trotskyist; the phrase meaning 'in a row' is read literally as the Trot's tab.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in succession, without a break, as in winning three games in a row.

clue.text: Wrong to accept kiss and clothing item like some adolescents

indicators.note: the word for wrong takes in the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a wrong is a sin
X is the conventional sign for a kiss
a tee is a T-shirt

explanation.surface: Teenagers' behaviour: misbehaving by letting in a kiss and a T-shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: XTEE sits between the I and N of SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aged that number is true of many teenagers, so it describes some adolescents.

clue.text: Food item is hot and cold? Something dodgy about that

indicators.note: the dodgy thing goes around the letters for 'is hot and cold'

parts.note: a fake is something not genuine, dodgy
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A dish served both hot and cold sounds suspect to a wary diner.
explanation.walkthrough: ISHC goes inside FAKE: F-ISHC-AKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A patty of fish and potato, fried in crumbs, is a common item of food.

clue.text: Very keen on the pub profits as well

parts.note: to be into something is to be enthusiastic about it
a bar is a pub
gain means profit, winnings

explanation.surface: Someone who loves the pub also cares about its takings.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means additionally, on top of everything else, just like 'besides'.

clue.text: Sixties musical with very good note (it's rather sharp)

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
pi (pious) is crossword slang for very good

explanation.surface: A review of a Sixties show with an excellent score, rather pointed in tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpin bend turns very tightly, so it is a sharp curve on a road.

clue.text: Article with zero volume included as part of Verdi chorus

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the volume letter is placed within the word for zero

parts.note: nil means zero

explanation.surface: Description of a recording of a Verdi chorus: the article, mute volume.
explanation.walkthrough: The Anvil Chorus is from Verdi's opera Il Trovatore.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Anvil Chorus is named after the smith's block, so that word is part of the chorus's title.

clue.text: Holland is besieged by alien — join the army

indicators.note: the Dutch code and 'is' are surrounded by the alien

parts.note: ET is the film's extra-terrestrial, so an alien
NL is the international code for the Netherlands

explanation.surface: With an alien siege on the Netherlands, it's time to sign up.
explanation.walkthrough: NL is the Netherlands' vehicle and country code, so Holland stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up for military service is to become a soldier.

clue.text: Way of manufacturing quote from stage performance?

definitions.meaning: an assembly line in a factory
a line spoken in a theatrical show

explanation.surface: A puzzling pairing of factory methods and theatre quotations.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory's assembly sequence is one sense; read literally, a line from a play or show is the other.

clue.text: Source of rubber unknown no longer?

parts.note: late means former, no longer with us
X is the mathematician's unknown

explanation.surface: Something that once was unknown is now known: the origin of rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: The milky sap of rubber trees is the raw material rubber is made from.

clue.text: Minister throttling one engaged in reversal of subsequent recovery

indicators.note: the minister and numeral are set within the other piece
the word for subsequent is read backwards

parts.note: later means subsequent

indicators.note: the minister grips the numeral by the throat, holding it inside

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A minister strangling someone during a later turnaround sounds like a rescue gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversal of' makes RETAL; 'throttling' gives RIEV; 'engaged in' sets RIEV inside RETAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting something back is its recovery, like the fetching of lost data.

clue.text: Imagine young child, daughter, lacking a little energy

indicators.note: lacking means one letter is missing from the combined pieces

parts.note: a preteen is a child just short of the teenage years
E is the abbreviation for energy, a little bit of it

explanation.surface: A parent pictures a small girl who is a bit short of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' drops one E from PRETEEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine can mean to make-believe, as children do when they play at being someone.

clue.text: Place with drinks around — fails to walk steadily

indicators.note: the drinks word goes around the place abbreviation

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A boozer surrounded by drinks can no longer walk straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tope' is an old word for drinking heavily, familiar mainly from crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps falling over is unsteady on their feet, failing to keep upright.

clue.text: Tendency to follow source about seasonal overhaul

indicators.note: the tendency word comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a spring is the source of a stream
C is circa, about
a leaning is a tendency

explanation.surface: A habit of tracing things back to their origins, applied to a yearly clean-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough cleaning of a house in the first months of the warmer season is a seasonal overhaul.

clue.text: Study picked up change almost entirely occurring at night

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, the study word read from bottom to top

parts.note: to con is to study
a turn is a change

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: all means entirely

explanation.surface: A student hears that a change is nearly complete and it happens after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reverses CON to NOC; 'almost' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls and bats are active after dark, so they are described as night-time creatures.

clue.text: Example of orderliness mostly brought to bear around recording

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the recording
mostly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: applied means brought to bear
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Tidiness achieved by putting a record on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' leaves APPLIE; 'around' wraps it round the recording.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'apple-pie order' means perfect neatness, so this dish is an example of orderliness.

clue.text: Strange precaution with mast? This isn't a hurricane!

indicators.note: strange means these letters are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Taking down the mast is overcautious: the weather isn't that bad.
explanation.walkthrough: PRECAUTION and MAST are mixed up together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a lot of fuss about something trivial, a tiny tempest rather than a real one.

clue.text: Salvage worker errs badly about encouragement to action

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the prompt
badly means the letters are arranged poorly, out of order

parts.note: a cue is a prompt to act

explanation.surface: A salvage man gets things wrong when urged to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' makes RESR, which 'about' wraps round the prompt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who saves people or goods from danger works at salvage.

clue.text: Chop up tree, but not the second, for instance

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to axe is to chop

indicators.note: the second letter of the tree is left out

parts.note: a maple is a tree

explanation.surface: Instructions to fell a tree, with a lumberjack's example given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' makes EXA from AXE; 'but not the second' drops the A of MAPLE, leaving MPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a case or specimen, a single illustration of something.

clue.text: Foreman providing slip with resistance

parts.note: a gaffe is a slip, a blunder
R is the symbol for resistance in physics

explanation.surface: A foreman makes a blunder and meets opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaffer' is British slang for a boss or foreman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a boss in charge of workers is called the gaffer, so a foreman.

clue.text: Place, back in Irish islands, working with handcrafts?

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the islands

parts.note: the Aran Islands lie off Ireland's west coast

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to sit is to place, set down

explanation.surface: A spot on an Irish island where craftworkers ply their trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives TIS; the Aran Islands, off Galway, are famous for their knitwear, which suits the craft surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual craftsperson works with their hands; the word also serves as an adjective, as in craft bread.

clue.text: Sum that would result in no change?

definitions.text: Sum that would result in no change?

parts.words: Sum that would result in no change?
parts.note: the phrase for adding up; in a down entry the small word read upwards is unchanged, being a palindrome

explanation.surface: An arithmetic question about a sum that leaves nothing different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot up' means add; but a tot written upwards, as a down answer is, reads the same, so turning it up changes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To add numbers together is to total them, the phrasal verb for calculating a sum.

clue.text: Gentle praise echoed after seizure reduced

indicators.note: the praise word is placed after the cut seizure word
reduced means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a grab is a seizure, a snatch

indicators.note: an echo sends the word back, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: Mild praise rings back after a snatch is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts GRAB to GRA; 'echoed' turns LAUD into DUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle slope rises slowly and steadily, like a gradual one.

clue.text: Cut it fine when cooking pasta

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are worked up into a new mix

explanation.surface: A warning about leaving little time to spare when making pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: These flat ribbon noodles are a type of Italian pasta.

clue.text: Young fellow consuming popular cheesecake?

indicators.note: the young fellow eats up the popular word, holding it inside

parts.note: a pup is a cheeky young man
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A lad tucking into a well-liked dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesecake is slang for glamour photographs of women, like a poster girl's picture.

clue.text: Fencer's ultimate skill lying in sword responses

indicators.note: ultimate means the last letter of the word
the skill word lies inside the sword

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword
art is skill

explanation.surface: A fencer's final flourish lies in swordplay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate' gives R; 'lying in' puts ART in EPEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Witty retorts and quick comebacks in conversation are replies of a sparkling kind.

clue.text: Clearly that is a measure of effort?

parts.note: well can mean clearly, plainly, as in 'well aware'

explanation.surface: A question about whether a sum quantifies how hard someone tried.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, to 'give it some welly' is to put in more effort; a wellie is a rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses 'welly' for force or effort, so it is a playful unit of exertion.
